alt_text: Photo in Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City. Text on the image: Talk about numbers like a pro
caption:
Numbers are where small grammar slips become big credibility problems. 'Rose by 12%' and 'rose to 12%' describe two very different results. Four phrases worth keeping for your next results meeting: • Revenue rose by 12%. ('by' = the size of the change)
• Costs remained flat. (no change at all)
• A slight dip in Q3. (a small, temporary fall)
• Year-on-year growth of 8%. ('of' = the amount of growth) A quick tip: the same idea works as a verb or a noun. 'Sales dipped slightly' and 'a slight dip in sales' say the same thing. Switching between them keeps your updates from sounding repetitive. Say the figure, name the period, and choose the word that matches the size of the movement.

slides.body: Four phrases for your next results meeting.
slides.headline: Talk about numbers like a pro

slides.body: Use 'by' for the size of the change. Use 'to' for the new figure: 'rose to 4.2 million'.
slides.headline: Revenue rose by 12%

slides.body: Pick small, precise words for small movements: flat, slight, steady. They keep your message in proportion.
slides.headline: Costs remained flat. A slight dip in Q3.

slides.body: After 'growth', use 'of' for the amount. 'Year-on-year' names the comparison period, so say it clearly.
slides.headline: Year-on-year growth of 8%

slides.body: Practise your results updates in English, using your own reports and your own meetings.
slides.headline: Present your numbers with confidence
